results.content: With three months to go until the U.S. midterm elections in November, voters increasingly seem to prefer Democrats over the Republican Party that has had control of Congress for the last two years. Results of a Reuters/Ipsos poll released Monday showed that 42% of registered voters would vote for a Democratic congressional candidate at present, compared to 37% for a Republican. The same survey also found that, for the first time in nearly a decade of its polling series, voters perceive the Democratic Party as having a better plan for the economy than the Republican Party. results.content: The 2026 Maine U.S. Senate race is becoming increasingly competitive, with a new Fox News poll showing Democratic candidate Troy Jackson holding a narrow lead over incumbent Republican Senator Susan Collins. The poll, conducted August 6-10, found Jackson ahead of Collins with 48 percent to 46 percent, putting the race within the poll's 3 percent margin of error and underscoring how closely contested the election could be. What To Know The latest numbers suggest a competitive race, but they don't necessarily signal immediate trouble for Collins.
